In this case, we have to use the identity  $1+{cot}^{2}⁡x={csc}^{2}⁡x.$ Rearranging this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{cot}^{2}⁡x & ={csc}^{2}⁡x-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2-\frac{x}{2}+2{cot}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (2-\frac{x}{2}+2({csc}^{2}⁡x-1))\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (2-\frac{x}{2}+2{csc}^{2}⁡x-2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (-\frac{x}{2}+2{csc}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-2\operatorname{cot}⁡x+C \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-2\operatorname{cot}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So we can use the identity 

$$
{tan}^{2}⁡x+1={sec}^{2}⁡x\,⟹\,{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}({x}^{2}{sec}^{2}⁡x-{x}^{2}{tan}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{x}^{2}({sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[{(\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3}-{0}^{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{{\pi }^{3}}{64} \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{192}\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we have to use the identity  $1+{cot}^{2}⁡x={csc}^{2}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}({sin}^{3}⁡x+{cot}^{2}⁡x{sin}^{3}⁡x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}{sin}^{3}⁡x(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}{sin}^{3}⁡x{csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}{sin}^{3}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We use the secant-tangent identity:

$$
{tan}^{2}⁡x+1={sec}^{2}⁡x\,⟹\,{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{6(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{6(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot (\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{6({sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x)}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{6\cdot 1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{6}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =6\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =6[\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{tan}⁡(0)] \\  & =6(1-0) \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$
